# build_autoinstall_iso

[← Command index](README.md)

Build an Ubuntu Server image that installs itself.

## Synopsis

```
build_autoinstall_iso [options]
```

## Description

Downloads the newest point release of the configured Ubuntu Server version, adds a
cloud-init seed that answers every installer question, and repacks it as an image
that boots from a USB stick (BIOS and UEFI) or a disc. Write it to a stick, boot the
target from it, and it installs without anyone at the keyboard.

Everything the installer would ask comes from `[UserData.Autoinstall]` in
`~/JoyBox.ini`: `autoinstall_version`, `autoinstall_username`, `autoinstall_realname`,
`autoinstall_hostname`, `autoinstall_ssh_keys` (comma-separated public keys),
`autoinstall_password_hash`, `autoinstall_locale`, `autoinstall_keyboard`,
`autoinstall_timezone`, `autoinstall_packages`, `autoinstall_serial_console` and
`autoinstall_overlay_file`. A build is refused unless there is a username the
installer accepts, a hostname, and at least one of a password hash or an SSH key.
Usernames the installer rejects only once it is running on the target, such as
`admin` or `operator`, are refused here instead.

The generated seed wipes the largest disk and lays it out as a 512 MB EFI partition
plus an ext4 root, creates the account with passwordless sudo, installs and enables
the SSH server with password logins disabled, and installs `autoinstall_packages`.
With no password hash the account's password is locked rather than empty.

Anything else the machine is for goes in an overlay: a YAML file merged into the
generated document, written either as a whole `autoinstall:` document or as just its
contents. Lists under `packages`, `snaps`, `early-commands`, `late-commands`, `users`,
`write_files` and `runcmd` are appended to rather than replaced, dictionaries merge key
by key, and plain values override. Late commands run in the installed system with the
network up but without a running systemd; anything that needs systemd belongs in
`user-data` `runcmd`, which runs on first boot. `Scripts/autoinstall/homelab_llm.yaml`
is a worked example for a GPU LLM server.

The download is checked against the `SHA256SUMS` published beside it, and that listing
is checked with gpg against `autoinstall_signing_keyring`
(`/usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg` by default), including that the
signing key is `autoinstall_signing_fingerprint` (the Ubuntu CD image signing key by
default). A download that fails either check is deleted. The seed goes in `/nocloud`
on the image, every boot entry gets `autoinstall ds=nocloud;s=/cdrom/nocloud/` before
its `---` separator, and the boot menu waits 2 seconds.

## Options

### Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Directory to write the image into, created if missing; the current directory when omitted. |
| `-n, --output_name <output_name>` | Filename of the image to write. Default: `ubuntu-autoinstall.iso`. |

### Source image

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-s, --source_iso <source_iso>` | Stock Ubuntu Server image to start from instead of downloading one; used without verification. |
| `-r, --release <release>` | Ubuntu release to build from, such as `24.04`, instead of `autoinstall_version`; the newest point release of it is used. |

### Seed

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-t, --hostname <hostname>` | Hostname for the installed machine, instead of `autoinstall_hostname`. |
| `-l, --serial_console` | Also send installer and kernel output to the serial console (`console=ttyS0`). |
| `-y, --overlay <overlay>` | YAML file merged into the generated autoinstall config, for extra packages, snaps, files and commands; `autoinstall_overlay_file` when omitted. |
| `-d, --user_data <user_data>` | Complete cloud-init user-data file to use as it is, instead of generating one. |
| `-w, --show_seed` | Print the user-data and meta-data this configuration produces, list what is missing, and stop without downloading anything. |

### Verification

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-k, --skip_verify` | Do not check the downloaded image against its published checksum, nor the checksum's signature. |
| `-g, --skip_signature` | Check the checksum but not who signed the published checksum listing. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Check the seed the configuration produces, without downloading

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso --show_seed
```

### Check the seed with an overlay applied

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso --show_seed -y Scripts/autoinstall/homelab_llm.yaml
```

### Build into the current directory

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso
```

### Build elsewhere, with a name and a hostname for this machine

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso -o ~/Images -n homelab.iso -t homelab
```

### Build the GPU LLM server image

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso -y Scripts/autoinstall/homelab_llm.yaml -t llm -n llm.iso
```

### Build from an image already on disk

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso -s ~/Downloads/ubuntu-24.04.1-live-server-amd64.iso
```

### Build from a complete cloud-init file of your own

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso -d ~/JoyBox/Autoinstall/user-data
```

### Go through the build without downloading or writing anything

```bash
build_autoinstall_iso -o ~/Images -p -v
```

## Notes

- Booting the image erases the target's largest disk without asking; there are 2 seconds at the boot menu to interrupt.
- Write it to a stick with `sudo dd if=ubuntu-autoinstall.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync`.
- The stock image is kept next to the output as `ubuntu-server-<version>.iso` and re-checked and reused by the next build. An image given with `--source_iso` is used as it is, without any check.
- If gpg or the keyring is missing the build stops rather than going on unverified; `--skip_signature` builds anyway, `--skip_verify` skips both checks.
- Make an SSH key with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/joybox_autoinstall` and put the `.pub` contents in `autoinstall_ssh_keys`. Make a password hash with `mkpasswd --method=SHA-512` or `openssl passwd -6`; it only matters at the console.
- With `--user_data` the file is used exactly as written: no account checks, and neither the overlay nor the profile's packages are applied. Only the hostname still goes into `meta-data`.
- Needs Gpg and XorrISO from `setup_tools`. Try the image in `boot_vm_image` before writing it to a stick.
